title.narrative: Coordinated Action on Disability in Liberia (CAD-L)
Coordinated Action on Disability in Liberia (CAD-L)

description.narrative:
AIFO är en internationell ickestatlig organisation baserad i Bologna, Italien med landskontor i Monrovia, Liberia. Projektet ”Coordinated Action on Disability in Liberia” (CAD-L) har en löptid från 1 september 2021 till 31 augusti 2025 med en total finansieringsram på 34 700 000 SEK. Sverige är ensam givare till projektet. Det övergripande målet för projektet är att 'persons with disabilities act as advocates and agents of change for an equitable and inclusive Liberia'. Projektets specifika övergripande mål är att 'Personer med funktionsvariation är till en större utsträckning ekonomiskt oberoende'. För att nå det specifika målet har tre delresultat identifierats;
1. Allmänheten har ändrad attityd till det socioekonomiska bidraget funktionsvarierade ger till Liberia
2. Sociala aktörer har ett definierat kollektivavtal om anständigt arbete för funktionsvarierande
3. Konkreta åtgärder som har vidtagits av ansvarsbärare och civilsamhällsorganisationer har skapat nya möjligheter för personer med funktionsvariation gällande sysselsättning, egenföretagande och entreprenörskap inom den offentliga och privata sektorn.

The contribution 'Coordinated Action on Disability in Liberia' (CAD-L) is a project by AIFO an International NGO based in Bologna Italy with country office in Monrovia, Liberia. The project has a duration 1 September 2021 to 31 August 2025 with a total funding envelop of 34 700 000 SEK of which Sweden is the sole donor. The overall goal of the project is 'persons with disabilities act as advocates and agents of change for an equitable and inclusive Liberia'. The project will directly fulfil the specific objective 'Persons with disabilities have improved economic independence'. In order to achieve its specific objectives, the project will achieve three intermediary outcomes: 1. The general public has changed attitudes towards the socio-economic contribution PWDs make to Liberia; 2. Social actors in Liberia are able to negotiate and conclude a collective agreement on decent work for PWDs and 3. Concrete steps taken by Duty Bearers and CSOs have created new opportunities for persons with disabilities employment, self-employment and entrepreneurship in the public and private sectors.

Project overall objective:
Persons with disabilities act as advocates and agents of change for an equitable and inclusive Liberia
Project specific objective:
PWDs have improved economic independence
INTERMEDIATE OUTCOME 1. The general public has changed attitudes towards the socio-economic contribution PWDs make to Liberia
INTERMEDIATE OUTCOME 2. Social actors have a defined collective agreement on decent work for PWDs
INTERMEDIATE OUTCOME 3. Concrete steps taken by Duty Bearers (DBs) and CSOs have created new opportunities for PWDs employment, self-employment and entrepreneurship in the public and private sectors

description.narrative:
Intermediate Outcome 1. The public has changed attitudes towards the socio-economic contribution PWDs make to Liberia
Results example 1: Journalists Network on Disability Reporting with Radio Campaigns
In YR3, OPDs teamed up with media outlets to create the Journalists Network on Disability Reporting, resulting in 22 impactful stories that improve disability journalism and promote positive representations of resilience. During the campaign, a total of 374 radio talk shows reached diverse audiences on PwD rights, with 26% of callers being female (207) and 74% male (601), highlighting the need for increased female participation.
Results example 2: Successful implementation of VIDEO CAMPAIGNS
The video campaign is transforming how society views of PWDs. Participants are pledging to embrace inclusion, actively involving PWDs in social development initiatives and not calling them by their disabilities. During this period, the video campaigns reach out to about 1000 participants directly benefited from five video campaigns, generating twice as many indirect benefits and showcasing our wide reaching impact.
The video campaign is a powerful tool to enhance the perception of Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) because it combines storytelling, emotion, and visibility to challenge stereotypes and shift public attitudes.
Video content can break down negative or limiting perceptions by showcasing PWDs as capable, talented, independent, and active contributors to society. It raises awareness and draws attention to the barriers PWDs face and how they overcome them, prompting conversations about inclusion, accessibility, and rights.
Bomi county had the highest attendance at 286, followed by Bong at 229, Lofa at 182, Nimba at 161, and Montserrado at 70. This suggests varying levels of engagement across counties, with Bomi showing the strongest turnout.
Three (3) roundtable dialogues were held: two (2) at the county level and 1 nationally led by NCD, NUOD, and stakeholders. All these were contributed to the output of awareness and sensitization campaign which will leave to public changed attitude toward social-economic development of PWDs.
INTERMEDIATE OUTCOME 2. Social actors have a defined collective agreement on decent work for PWDs
Results example 3: strengthen and support to tripartite and held first National Conference for disability inclusive labour, decent work and social protection made.
The project continue to support the tripartite social pratners in Liberia )The Government, trade unions and employers organization). Three 3 meetings out of 6 held and supported the Ministry of Labour with office materials, on the sectoral consultations, three were held in the agriculture, tertiary and security sectors. As part of the result for social dialogue, the first ever national conference was held in Liberia with the participation representatives from the projects counties, line ministries, human rights organizations, NGOs/CSOs, OPDs, partners of the project and the donors community. This shows significant advancement in social dialogue as success stories indicate that in Bomi - NASSCORP employed 1 physically challenged. The Superintendent office employed 2 persons with disabilities, one female and one male. At the county office for the ministry of Education employed 2 persons with disabilities. In Lofa, installation of ramp at the administrative building has been completed with one person with disabilities employed at the Superintendent Office. PwDs themselves have reported positive lifestyle shifts because of knowledge from decent work workshops. A visually impaired female established vegetable garden and encourages other PwDs to join her
INTERMEDIATE OUTCOME 3. Concrete steps taken by Duty Bearers (DBs) and CSOs have created new opportunities for PWDs employment, self-employment and entrepreneurship in the public and private sectors
Results example 4: Start-ups: Women and men with disabilities run successful startups
A total of 33 startups across the five counties were mentored and coached during year three of the project. For example in Nimba county, seven startups were monitored, covering different business sectors such as timber, soap production, agriculture, honey production, and trading (red oil and water sales). In montserrado, a total of eight startups were monitored, covering different business sectors such as agriculture (crops and livestock), food processing, soap production, retail and trading, handicrafts and artisanal products. In Lofa, six startups were monitored in the Voijama, Kolahun, and Foyah districts and they are involved in agriculture (rice farming), soap production, livestock and food processing. Bomi county had a total of three startups were monitored in Bomi County, covering business sectors such as beverage sales, soap production, and rice trading. Lastly in Bong county, a total of nine startups, These startups reflect a diverse range of sectors, including agriculture, manufacturing, services, and trade, contributing to the local economy in Bong County.
According to Victoria Country Cloth, though established in 2021 was on the verge of collapsing, the opportunity given by CAD-L project in 2023 through a grant of US$2000 enabled her Business to get revived. Following the receipt of the grant her team go on board 4 additional persons with disability who had undergone training in weaving and are now performing adequately in the manufacturing of country cloth. For Victoria, working with and empowering other PWDs is a dream come through, as through this process, income generated has helped members of the group have their children retained in school compared to before when the kids were sent home due to lack of school fees.
The Start-up has become one of the sole suppliers of country clothes in Voinjama and its environment hereby enabling several members some of whom were begging around to keep involved with a more dependable and stable act of production of the county cloth from which they can make ends meet and support themselves and their family. Out of the US$2,000 received from AIFO Victoria and her team have translated their usual open weaving production site into a weaving production now carried out under a newly constructed hall in which they are more certain to continue their work both during the rain and dry. "Nothing makes us happier than seeing ourselves involved in a business that supports not only PWDs but persons with abilities as well. We feel respected and honored by what we do and are doing all possible to ensure this is long lasting. Today the Victoria women has produced more than 100 lappers sets which has been sold in and out of Lofa. The team is currently working on their market linkage to enhance sales. A special thanks to AIFO and her parters for the support "
